\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{باحث} (bāḥith)}{باحث (bāḥith)}]{\ar{باحث} (bāḥith) — a researcher}

\label{lesson:AR-C391-bahith}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a scholarship, then the Arabic for to enrol.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{باحث}}
\textbf{\ar{باحث}} — \emph{bāḥith} — \textquotedblleft{}a researcher\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يعمل} \ar{الباحث} \ar{في} \ar{الجامعة} \ar{منذ} \ar{سنوات}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yaʿmalu al-bāḥith fī al-jāmiʿa mundhu sanawāt.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The researcher has worked at the university for years.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{باحث}} (\emph{bāḥith}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{b-ḥ-th}, \textquotedblleft{}to dig, to search\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Bāḥith} is the active participle of \emph{baḥatha}, to search: a researcher.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bāḥith}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bāḥith}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yaʿmalu al-bāḥith fī al-jāmiʿa mundhu sanawāt.} — The researcher has worked at the university for years.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a scholarship, then the Arabic for to enrol, then say \emph{bāḥith} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{دراسة} (dirāsa)}{دراسة (dirāsa)}]{\ar{دراسة} (dirāsa) — a study}

\label{lesson:AR-C391-dirasa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to enrol, then the Arabic for a researcher.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{دراسة}}
\textbf{\ar{دراسة}} — \emph{dirāsa} — \textquotedblleft{}a study\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{قرأت} \ar{دراسة} \ar{عن} \ar{النوم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{qaraʾtu dirāsa ʿan an-nawm.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I read a study about sleep.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{دراسة}} (\emph{dirāsa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{d-r-s}, \textquotedblleft{}to wear away; to study\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Dirāsa} is a verbal noun of \emph{darasa}, to study: studying, a study.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for giving reasons and opinions.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مختبر} (mukhtabar)}{مختبر (mukhtabar)}]{\ar{مختبر} (mukhtabar) — a laboratory}

\label{lesson:AR-C391-mukhtabar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a researcher, then the Arabic for a study.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مختبر}}
\textbf{\ar{مختبر}} — \emph{mukhtabar} — \textquotedblleft{}a laboratory\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يعمل} \ar{أخي} \ar{في} \ar{مختبر} \ar{كبير}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yaʿmalu akhī fī mukhtabar kabīr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مختبر}} (\emph{mukhtabar}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{kh-b-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to know thoroughly, to test\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Mukhtabar} is a noun of place from Form VIII \emph{ikhtabara}, to test: a place for testing, a laboratory.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for giving reasons and opinions.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{معهد} (maʿhad)}{معهد (maʿhad)}]{\ar{معهد} (maʿhad) — an institute}

\label{lesson:AR-C391-mahad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a study, then the Arabic for a laboratory.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{معهد}}
\textbf{\ar{معهد}} — \emph{maʿhad} — \textquotedblleft{}an institute\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{درست} \ar{الموسيقى} \ar{في} \ar{معهد} \ar{صغير}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{darastu al-mūsīqā fī maʿhad ṣaghīr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I studied music at a small institute.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{معهد}} (\emph{maʿhad}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-h-d}, \textquotedblleft{}to enjoin; to know a place\textquotedblright{} (Lane). A \emph{maʿhad} is a place one knows and comes back to; in modern use, an institute.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{استبيان} (istibyān)}{استبيان (istibyān)}]{\ar{استبيان} (istibyān) — a questionnaire}

\label{lesson:AR-C391-istibyan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a laboratory, then the Arabic for an institute.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{استبيان}}
\textbf{\ar{استبيان}} — \emph{istibyān} — \textquotedblleft{}a questionnaire\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ملأ} \ar{الطلاب} \ar{استبيانا} \ar{قصيرا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{malaʾa aṭ-ṭullāb istibyānan qaṣīran.}

\textbf{\ar{استبيان}} (\emph{istibyān}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{b-y-n}, \textquotedblleft{}to be apart; to become clear\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Istibyān} is a Form X verbal noun, seeking to make a thing clear: a questionnaire.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
